title: Feedback on My Intro/ Ship Sinking sequence?
author: SocialContractGuy
selftext:
Trying to walk the line between an engaging start that doesn’t drag too long but enough for users to care and want to keep playing.   
[Washed Ashore](https://thesocialcontractgame.com) 

I'm not a programmer, so I built *Washed Ashore* by working with AI as a collaborator. I acted as the designer and director. I decided what the story should be, how it should feel on a phone, and which choices should come back to haunt the player. I described all of that in plain language to Claude Code, an AI coding assistant, and it wrote the game's code. Almost every scene started with me playing the game and noticing something: a camera that pointed at the captain's legs, a character whose hands went through his coat, flags that looked like flat cards. Sometimes it was an idea, like the old man's walking stick washing ashore and upsetting the little girl. I'd send a screenshot or a sentence, and the AI would build it, test it in a browser, and show me a picture before anything went live. For characters, animals and props, I used Meshy, an AI 3D-model generator. The assistant asked me first every time, because each model cost credits. I also mixed in free hand-made art and sound packs from Kenney. To keep it safe, I set firm rules: every change went on its own branch and reached the live game only when I said "merge," players' saved progress could never be broken, and every change had to pass automated checks first. The AI did the technical work, but the vision, the taste and the final say were always mine.
